newsitem.title: USA: Fla. early/mid orange harvest ends on hot,dry note.
newsitem.headline: Fla. early/mid orange harvest ends on hot,dry note.

text.p: Dry weather conditions and high temperatures swept through Florida's citrus belt as the harvest of early and mid oranges came to a close, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.
Freeze-damaged and young Valencias, meanwhile, continue to move to processors and for fresh shipments.
An abundance of new growth on trees of all ages was also noted, and many groves are in or have completed their full bloom stage, FASS said.
Temperatures for the week ended March 9 neared 90 degrees Fahrenheit during the first part and then eased by about 10 degrees for the remainder of the week.
FASS reported an estimated 5,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended March 9, down from 18,000 boxes the previous week and 41,000 boxes in the week ended February 23.
An estimated 2,157,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended March 9, down from 3,818,000 boxes the prior week and 5,235,000 boxes the week ended February 23, FASS said.
